description: Opt-in: register a scheduled task that runs this bucket's Update-Package '*' after Windows Update installs updates (System log, WindowsUpdateClient Event ID 19). Idempotent; reversed by uninstalling.
notes: Install from an ELEVATED shell (e.g. 'sudo scoop install MarkMichaelis/UpdateBucketOnWindowsUpdate'): the task runs as you with highest privileges, which Windows only lets an elevated session register.
Task: \MarkMichaelis.ScoopBucket\UpdateBucketOnWindowsUpdate. Inspect with 'Get-ScheduledTask -TaskPath \MarkMichaelis.ScoopBucket\' or Task Scheduler.
Log: %LOCALAPPDATA%\MarkMichaelis.ScoopBucket\UpdateBucketOnWindowsUpdate\UpdateBucketOnWindowsUpdate.log (rotated at 1 MB; one .1 generation kept).

Defender definition updates and Microsoft Store app updates also raise Event ID 19 several times a day; the runner skips the bucket update when those are the only updates installed since its last check.

A failed bucket update is not retried automatically: the run exits 1 (see Last Run Result and the log), and the next qualifying Windows update retries it. To retry now: & "$env:ProgramData\MarkMichaelis.ScoopBucket\UpdateBucketOnWindowsUpdate\Invoke-BucketUpdateAfterWindowsUpdate.ps1" -Force
The task runs only while you are logged on (no stored password); an update installed while logged off is picked up by the next Windows Update event after logon.

The runner is copied to %ProgramData%\MarkMichaelis.ScoopBucket\UpdateBucketOnWindowsUpdate so an unelevated process cannot rewrite what runs elevated. It still imports MarkMichaelis.ScoopBucket from the scoop bucket clone, which is as writable as your scoop install.

script: if (((Get-PSCallStack).Command -contains 'update_app') -or (Get-Variable -Name old_version -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Write-Host 'scoop update in progress: skipping uninstaller (#401).'; return }
